edges.reason: _msgSender() returns the untrusted msg.sender value.
Ownable constructor assigns _owner from _msgSender(), establishing the privileged account.
newComer is initialized from _msgSender() at declaration and is the address checked by onlyOwner.
Constructor credits the whole _tTotal to _balances[_msgSender()].
transfer delegates all balance movement to _transfer.
transferFrom delegates balance movement to _transfer.
transferFrom re-approves the reduced allowance via _approve.
transferFrom subtracts amount from _allowances[sender][_msgSender()].
approve forwards _msgSender(), spender and amount to _approve.
_transfer reads and writes the _balances mapping for sender and recipient.
_transfer performs sub/add on balances, relying on SafeMath for overflow safety.
_approve writes _allowances[ol][tt], sometimes force-zeroing it for non-owners.
_approve compares ol against owner() to decide whether to zero the allowance.
renounceOwnership sets _owner to address(0) under onlyOwner.
transferOwnership replaces _owner with newOwner under onlyOwner.
onlyOwner modifier gates renounceOwnership on newComer, which may differ from _owner.
onlyOwner modifier gates transferOwnership on newComer, which may differ from _owner.
sendValue executes recipient.call{value: amount}("") in an unchecked external invocation.
_functionCallWithValue executes target.call{value: weiValue}(data) on an arbitrary target.
A malicious recipient can re-enter token transfer logic during the value-bearing external call.

normalization_plan.reason: sender is the debit-side address parameter consumed directly by _transfer.
recipient is the credit-side address parameter consumed directly by _transfer.
amount is the value parameter used by _transfer when updating _balances.
ol is the owner address parameter written into _allowances by _approve.
tt is the spender address parameter written into _allowances by _approve.
spender is the delegatee parameter forwarded by approve to _approve.
newOwner is the address parameter assigned to _owner.
local success only holds the boolean result of the low-level value call.
